_comment: Dispatch-template PARAMS: what a template asks a caller to fill, parsed the
same way on both providers.
`library.list` advertises a machine-readable `params` list on every kind
'dispatch' item so a Fleet Manager can learn a template's placeholders without
fetching the whole library and reading its markdown. BOTH providers answer that
call — the desktop's hubCapabilities.ts under a local client, cmd/brain under
the default catalog delegation (every web/mobile/MCP caller) — so the parser now
exists twice, and a caller must not learn a different param set depending on
which one ran.
THE HARD RULE THIS ENCODES, from dispatchTemplate.ts's header: a placeholder is
REQUIRED BY DEFAULT. `{{task}}` refuses the spawn when unfilled; only the
author's explicit `{{task:default}}` makes one optional. So `required` is not a
hint — it is the difference between a dispatch that fails loudly and one that
silently ships boilerplate with an empty task slot. Advertising it wrong is
worse than not advertising it.
THE DRIFT THIS EXISTS TO CATCH is whitespace. dispatchTemplate.ts spells the
token with JavaScript's `\s` and trims with String.prototype.trim(), and
NEITHER of Go's obvious equivalents is that set: regexp `\s` is only
[\t\n\f\r ] (no vertical tab, no NBSP), while strings.TrimSpace/unicode.IsSpace
adds U+0085 NEL that JS does not trim and omits U+FEFF that JS does. A template
padded with any of those would parse to a DIFFERENT param name on one provider
— a name the caller then cannot fill, and only on some clients. The four exotic
cases below are the whole reason dispatchparams.go writes the class out by hand
instead of reaching for \s.
Order is normative: params come back in FIRST-SEEN order, and the first
occurrence of a name wins, because each token is resolved independently at
render time and the first spelling is the one a reader of the listing acts on.
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be declared
here and everything here must be a block. Held by cmd/brain/corpusvocab_test.go
and apps/desktop/src/main/services/contractsVocabulary.test.ts.

cases.why: One template body in, one ordered param list out. Both parsers must produce this array exactly — same names, same order, same required flags, same defaults.

owners.apps/desktop/src/main/lib/dispatchTempla: dispatchTemplateParams (TS) — the copy the desktop provider's library.list publishes, and the copy whose sibling renderDispatchTemplate then ENFORCES on spawn. This side is normative: the Go twin is written to match it, whitespace class included.
owners.services/hub/cmd/brain/dispatchparams.go: dispatchTemplateParams (Go) — the copy cmd/brain's library.list publishes for every web/mobile/MCP caller under the default catalog delegation. It parses but never renders: agents.spawn's `template` param stays declined here (parity_test.go spawnParamsDeclined).

cases.name: a bare placeholder is required
cases.why: The regression floor and the whole hard rule: a bare token is REQUIRED, so a spawn that omits it is refused rather than rendered with an empty task slot.

cases.name: an explicit default makes it optional
cases.why: The only way a placeholder becomes optional is the author writing one. `default` is the text the render actually substitutes, so a caller can see what it gets by omitting the param.

cases.name: required and optional, in first-seen order
cases.why: The shipped ship-task shape. Order is normative — a caller reads the list top-down to fill it.

cases.name: the {{cwd}} auto var is never advertised
cases.why: cwd is filled by the HOST from the spawn's own cwd. Advertising it would invite a caller to pass a value for a slot it does not own, and the render prefers the caller's value on a name collision.

cases.name: an auto var with a default is still not advertised
cases.why: The auto-var exclusion is on the NAME, before the default is considered — otherwise `{{cwd:/tmp}}` would smuggle cwd back onto the advertised list by adding a colon.

cases.name: the prompt-var '?' spelling parses identically
cases.why: A template authored for the renderer's insert dialog must advertise the same params here; the leading '?' is stripped, not part of the name.

cases.name: first occurrence wins — bare first stays required
cases.why: Each token is resolved independently at render time, so the bare one still refuses an unfilled spawn. Advertising it as optional because a later token has a default would promise a default the render will not honor.

cases.name: first occurrence wins — default first stays optional
cases.why: The mirror direction, pinned so nobody 'fixes' the rule into last-wins or into required-wins. It is FIRST-seen, in both directions.

cases.name: only the first colon splits
cases.why: A default may contain colons — git refs and URLs do. Splitting on the last colon would silently truncate the default.

cases.name: an empty default is optional, not required
cases.why: `{{note:}}` is the author explicitly saying 'may be omitted, renders as nothing'. Treating an empty default as absent would flip it to required and start refusing spawns that are correct.

cases.name: padding inside the braces is trimmed
cases.template: {{  task  }} and {{  delivery : open a PR  }}
cases.why: Ordinary ASCII padding, including around the colon, must not become part of the name or the default — a name with a stray space is one templateParams cannot address.

cases.name: vertical tab padding is whitespace
cases.why: U+000B is in JavaScript's \s and NOT in Go's regexp \s. A Go copy that used \s would advertise the param as "\u000btask", which no caller can fill.

cases.name: no-break space padding is whitespace
cases.why: U+00A0 is in JavaScript's \s and not in Go's regexp \s. It is also the space a template author gets by accident from a word processor or a copied web page.

cases.name: a BOM inside the braces is whitespace
cases.why: U+FEFF is trimmed by String.prototype.trim() and NOT by strings.TrimSpace/unicode.IsSpace — the direction where Go is narrower than JS, and the one a TrimSpace-based port gets wrong.

cases.name: U+0085 NEL is NOT whitespace
cases.why: The direction where Go is WIDER than JS: unicode.IsSpace trims U+0085 and JavaScript does not. The advertised name keeps it, because the renderer's own token match keeps it — the listing must describe the parser that will actually run, not a tidier one.

cases.name: an empty token declares nothing
cases.why: A token with no name (or only whitespace) is skipped rather than advertised as a param named "", which nothing could fill and which would make every template look like it wanted an anonymous value.

cases.name: a template with no placeholders has no params
cases.template: Just prose. No slots at all.
cases.why: An empty list is a real answer — 'this template is ready to dispatch as-is' — and must not be confused with 'the parser found nothing because it broke'.

cases.name: a duplicate name is listed once
cases.why: The list is DISTINCT names in first-seen order; a template that repeats a slot asks for one value, not three.
